title: Fractional Alerting and Noise Reduction Strategy for Platform Services
author: Elena Park
summary: A practical design and rollout guide for reducing alert noise across Redwood's platform by adopting fractional alerting, routed escalation, and dashboard-driven feedback loops.
body:
Overview

This document describes a unified approach ("fractional alerting") to reduce operational noise while preserving fast detection of user-impacting regressions across Redwood's platform services. It complements existing alert routing and escalation playbooks by providing: an alert taxonomy, rule-design templates, dashboard bundles, rollout checklist, and success metrics for iterative tuning.

Goals

- Reduce actionable alert volume by 55% for platform-owned services in the next quarter.
- Ensure mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for P1 service-impact alerts remains < 5 minutes.
- Preserve at least 95% precision for alerts that trigger automated remediation.

Scope

- Applies to services owned by the Platform team (see ownership matrix).
- Covers infra-level observability (compute, networking, storage), serving-runtime health (KV cache pressure, batch backpressure, model-fallbacks), and platform orchestration (autoscaler failures, control-plane errors).
- Does NOT include customer-specific product endpoints (handled by product teams' alerting playbooks).

Why fractional alerting?

Traditional binary alerts (on/off) create a flood of low-impact notifications. Fractional alerting groups indicators into graded signals that map to different response pathways:

- Fraction 0 (Informational): metrics that are useful for trend analysis only. No paging.
- Fraction 1 (Operational): symptoms that should appear on team dashboards and Slack #ops but do not page.
- Fraction 2 (Actionable): issues requiring oncall attention (pages) and an SRE-runbook.
- Fraction 3 (Service-impact): P1s—user-facing outages or data-loss risks that trigger immediate paging, incident commander assignment, and status page updates.

Design principles

1) Metric-first: Each alert maps to a single SLI with a documented SLO and a clarity note (what false positives look like).
2) Topology-aware thresholds: Thresholds are scaled by instance count and queue depth to avoid noisy triggers during rolling deploys.
3) Context-rich payloads: Page messages must include origin-host, recent 1h trend, top-3 correlated traces, and suggested next steps.
4) Safe automation: Any automated remediation must start in Fraction 1 or 2 with a manual approval gate before promotion to Fraction 3.

Alert taxonomy and examples

Below are canonical templates. Replace service names/metric names with actual Prometheus/Datadog identifiers.

| Fraction | Trigger | Threshold (example) | Response | Route |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Cache hit ratio drift | 7-day deviation > 6% | Dashboard annotation | #platform-observe (no page) |
| 1 | Sustained error spike (non-5xx) | > 5% of requests in 10m window | Slack notification, update incident board | #platform-ops (no page) |
| 2 | Queue backlog growth | backlog > 2x steady-state for 5m | Pager to oncall, runbook run | Pager -> platform-oncall |
| 3 | Request p99 latency > SLO & error rate > 1% | p99 > 500ms AND errors > 1% for 3m | Immediate page, incident declared | Pager -> incident-manager + #inc-comm

Alert rule templates (Prometheus-style pseudocode)

1) Fraction-2 queue backlog example:

```
alert: PlatformQueueBacklog_Sustained
expr: (sum(queue_length{service="model-router"}) by (cluster) > 2 * avg_over_time(sum(queue_length{service="model-router"})[1h]))
for: 5m
labels:
  fraction: "2"
  severity: "major"
annotations:
  summary: "Sustained queue backlog on model-router cluster {{ $labels.cluster }}"
  runbook: "https://confluence/internal/runbooks/model-router-backlog"
```

2) Fraction-3 combined-signal example:

```
alert: ServingLateHighErrors_Combined
expr: (increase(request_errors_total{service="serving"}[3m]) / increase(requests_total{service="serving"}[3m])) > 0.01
and
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="serving"}[3m])) by (le)) > 0.5
for: 3m
labels:
  fraction: "3"
  severity: "critical"
annotations:
  summary: "Serving service has crossed error and latency thresholds"
  action: "Page oncall, failover to model-variant-b if available"
```

Routing and escalation rules

- Fraction mapping -> page policy: Fraction 2 pages the primary platform oncall rotation. Fraction 3 pages primary + on-call secondary and automatically assigns an incident commander from the Platform incident-response roster.
- Auto-silence window: Alerts tagged as Fraction 1 or 0 should never page and are silenced during deploy windows (deploy detection is a separate signal; see rollout checklist).
- Deduplication policy: Alerts with > 50% overlapping affected hosts in a 2m window are deduplicated into a single incident with aggregated context.

Dashboards and views to deploy

1) Platform Health Overview (shared): SLO burn, cluster-level p50/p95/p99, error rate heatmap, active incidents.
2) Fractional Alert Queue: a time-series view of alerts by fraction to track noise trends.
3) Runbook Execution Panel: recent runbook runs and outcome (success/failure/manual).
4) Canary Release Monitor: deploys vs alert counts in last 30m.

Implementation & rollout plan (8 weeks)

Week 0: Kickoff & discovery
- Inventory all existing alerts for platform-owned services (CSV export). Owner: Observability team.
- Identify top 200 noisy alerts by volume in last 90 days.

Week 1–2: Taxonomy mapping and SLI alignment
- Map noisy alerts to SLIs and SLOs. Create a "clarity note" for each alert.
- Tag alerts with provisional fraction (0–3).

Week 3–4: Rule consolidation and dedup logic
- Implement deduplication and topology-aware scaling.
- Add context enrichment for pages (trace links, recent deploy IDs).

Week 5: Canary rollout (10% services)
- Deploy fractional routing for a small set of low-risk services.
- Monitor Fractional Alert Queue and adjust thresholds.

Week 6–7: Expand to all platform services
- Gradual 25% -> 50% -> 100% rollout with 48h monitoring windows.

Week 8: Retrospective and SLAs update
- Measure reduction in actionable pages, MTTA, and precision of automated remediation.
- Publish findings and next steps.

Rollback and safety gates

- Emergency revert label: any service owner can roll back fractional routing for their service with a single-command in orchestration (documented in runbook).
- Auto-revert condition: if Fraction-3 pages increase by >20% week-over-week during rollout, auto-disable fractional routing and alert Observability.

Success metrics and dashboards to track

- Actionable page rate (pages / service / day) — target: -55% vs baseline.
- MTTA for Fraction-3 — target: < 5 minutes.
- False positive rate on automated remediations — target: < 5%.
- Signal-to-noise ratio (fraction 2+3 pages / total alerts) — target: improve by 2x.

Ownership matrix

| Area | Primary owner | Secondary |
|---|---|---|
| Alert rule lifecycle | Observability team | Platform reliability engineers |
| Pager routing & escalation | Oncall tooling team | Platform SRE lead |
| Dashboards | Platform metrics team | Developer experience |
| Runbook maintenance | Service owners | Observability docs |

Operational play examples (quick checklist)

1) On page receipt (Fraction 2):
   1. Acknowledge within 10 minutes.
   2. Confirm if it affects customer-facing traffic.
   3. Run recommended runbook steps; capture outcome in incident ticket.

2) On page receipt (Fraction 3):
   1. Immediate ack and assign incident commander.
   2. Post status update to status.redwood.ai and #inc-comm.
   3. Execute failover or rollback plan if applicable.

Retrospective cadence

- Bi-weekly noise review: share platform fractional alert queue trends, top noisy rules, and adjustments made.
- Quarterly postmortem: for any rollouts that hit the auto-revert condition.

Related runbooks & references

- Model router backlog runbook: https://confluence/internal/runbooks/model-router-backlog
- Platform oncall rota & incident roster: https://confluence/internal/teams/platform-oncall
- Existing routing playbook (for cross-reference): /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/platform-alert-routing-and-escalation-playbook-2026

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets

- Export alerts to CSV (Datadog example):

```
ddpy alert list --query "tags:platform" --format csv > platform-alerts.csv
```

- Quick silence during deploy (one-liner using alert-manager API):

```
curl -XPOST http://alert-manager/api/silences -d '{"matchers": [{"name":"team","value":"platform"}], "startsAt":"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)", "endsAt":"$(date -u -d "+10 minutes" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"}'
```
